source_text: Ι. Βουληϑέντι σοι zart ἀχρίβειαν ἐχμαϑεῖν τὰ προτεϑέντα ὑπι σοῦ ἡμῖν κεφάλαια, ἀγαπητέ μου ἀδελφὲ Θεόφιλε, εὔλογον ἡγησάμην, ἀφϑόνως ἀρυσάμενος ὡς ἐὲ ἁγίας πηγῆς ἐξ αὐτῶν τῶν ϑείων γραφῶν καταστῆσαί σοι κατ᾽ ὀφϑαλμὸν τὰ ζητούμενα" ἵνα μὴ μόνον ταῖς τῶν ὥτων ἀχοαῖς ἐγκαταϑέμενος ταῦτα εὐφρανϑῆς, ἀλλὰ δυνάμει καὶ αὐτὰ τὰ πράγϊματα ἐνιστορήσας κατὰ πάντα τὸν ϑεὸν δοξάσαι δυνηϑῆς.
pass_a_gloss: You having wished to learn the precision of the things proposed by you to us, my beloved brother Theophilus, I considered it reasonable, having drawn abundantly as if from a holy spring from the divine scriptures themselves, to set before your eyes the things being sought, so that not only having been entrusted to the ears' hearing, you may be delighted by these things, but also, having been instructed by the power of the things themselves, you may be able to glorify God in every way.

choices.why: more accurate rendering of the Greek participle
included to maintain the original phrase

pass_b_english: Since you wished to learn the precise details of the topics you proposed to us, my beloved brother Theophilus, I considered it reasonable to set the matters you seek before your eyes, drawing abundantly from the divine Scriptures themselves as from a holy spring. I did this so that you would not only delight in these things by hearing them with your ears, but also, having been instructed by the power of the realities themselves, you might be able to glorify God in every way.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly render the complex participial structure and the metaphor of the holy spring. The Greek 'ταῖς τῶν ὥτων ἀχοαῖς' is rendered as 'ears' hearing' in A and 'hearing them with your ears' in B, both faithful. No omissions or contradictions found.
